newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Shell/Mobil to build Australian used oil plant.
newsitem.headline: Shell/Mobil to build Australian used oil plant.

text.p: Waste oil recycler Transpacific Industries Pty Ltd said on Friday it had formed a joint venture company with the local units of Royal Dutch Shell and Mobil Corp to build a A$10 million used oil lubricants plant.
Transpacific said it would have a 50 percent stake in the new company, Nationwide Oil Pty Ltd, with the two oil majors each owning 25 percent.
It said A$7 million would be spent on a kit plant from Interline Resources Corp with the remainder to be spent on plant infrastructure at Wetherill Park, west of Sydney.
Nationwide Oil managing director Grant Fortescue told Reuters that the plant would produce between 25 million and 30 million litres annually and be commissioned in November this year.
Shell and Mobil would be responsible for marketing the used oil products which Fortescue said could be used in the industrial lubrications market or blended into auto distillates.
He said the plant was the first of its kind in Australia and the fourth to be built by Interline, with the others in Dubai, the United Kingdom, and South Korea.
